newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Serbian opposition offended by Dini.
newsitem.headline: Serbian opposition offended by Dini.

text.p: Serbia's opposition coalition attacked Italian Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini on Friday for urging them to back away from demands in a dispute with the government that has sparked four weeks of mass protests.
Vuk Draskovic, one of the leaders of the opposition Zajedno (Together) coalition, told a news conference he was "surprised and offended" by Dini's comments in Belgrade on Thursday.

Dini met Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic and then the Zajedno leaders in a bid to find a settlement to the crisis over the ruling Socialist party's annulment of local elections the opposition says it won.

"Reinstatement of results (of the November 17 poll) seems to me to be something that is not on the cards as the basis for dialogue between the parties. They must find a formula around the impasse," Dini said after the talks.
Draskovic said the opposition leaders were outraged at the suggestion they drop their most basic demand.

"Such statements produce confusion and misunderstandings around the world, and he helped Milosevic act against democratic forces. He helped these acts of terror against the electoral will of the people of Serbia," Draskovic said.
Zajedno has insisted that the election results are not negotiable.
Dini denied in an interview with the Rome Daily La Repubblica that the simplest solution to the crisis would be for Milosevic to step down.
"No, absolutely. Milosevic does not intend to step down and I told the opposition clearly that this is not what the international community seeks," Dini said.
He said the only way out of the impasse was "a political solution which allows for the establishment of solid rules for the future. Above all for the elctions to be held next year".
Dini said he had not taken sides in favour of Milosevic and against the opposition.
He read Milosevic a one-page declaration of condemnation by the international community.

"Then, I told him very clearly that he must find a way out of this situation otherwise his country would remain isolated. He must find a way to overcome the impasse and that way can only be dialogue," Dini said.
